node.title: General star records do not universally inject into minimal trades
node.closure: exact finite-field counterexample and complete census
node.statement: On D=F_17^*, the disjoint pair P={1,2,3}, Q={4,5,14} is a general order-1 width-3 star-PTE record but is not minimal and contains no width-2 minimal subrecord. Exhaustively, D has 4576 unordered general order-1 width-3 records, while its entire unordered F-4 minimal ledger has only 963 records over widths 1,...,8 (843 over widths 2,...,8). Hence no scale-free multiplicity-one injection from all general star records into all minimal records exists, and subset peeling also fails. This is not an official-row or strip-aware counterexample: n=16 and |F|=17<n^2, so x4 coverage may still use official-row first-owner strips or a broadened general-record u1 ledger.
